header: A small memory for the live routes. Each answer is kept for a while, so that many people opening the same card in a minute cost the other site one request. When the other site fails, I return the LAST GOOD answer with `stale: true` and its own time, so that the card can say "as of 3:10 pm, the source is not answering now" instead of showing nothing, or showing an old number as new. On a serverless host the memory lives only as long as the running instance: that is fine, because it is a courtesy, not a store. Nothing about any user is kept.

members.name: at
doc: When the value was fetched (ms since the epoch).

members.name: stale
doc: True when the other site failed and this is the last good answer.

symbols.name: memo
symbols.sig: export async function memo<T>(key: string, ttlMs: number, load: () => Promise<T>, now: () => number = Date.now): Promise<Memoised<T>>

symbols.name: inflight
doc: SERVE-THEN-REFRESH. For an answer that costs seconds to make (a news tab), nobody should wait for it when an older one is at hand. The entry has three ages:
- fresh (younger than `ttlMs`): returned as it is;

- REFRESH-AHEAD (older than `aheadAt` of the ttl, say 80%): returned at once, and a new one is made in the background (`schedule` keeps it alive on a serverless host: next/server's after()), so that in a busy hour nobody ever meets an expired entry;
- STALE (older than the ttl but younger than `maxStaleMs`): returned at once, the new one made in the background the same way;
- too old, or nothing kept: made now, the caller waits (and, if that fails, gets the old one marked stale, as `memo` does).
Only one refresh runs for a key at a time, however many ask.

members.name: maxStaleMs
doc: How long an old answer may still be served while a new one is made (default: three hours).

members.name: aheadAt
doc: The part of the ttl after which a refresh starts in the background while the answer is still served (default 0.8).

members.name: schedule
doc: Keeps a background job alive after the response has gone (next/server `after`); without it the job simply runs.

members.name: refreshing
doc: True when a new answer is being made in the background and this one is the one before it.

symbols.name: memoSwr
symbols.sig: export async function memoSwr<T>(key: string, ttlOf: number | ((kept: T) => number), load: () => Promise<T>, opts: SwrOptions = {}): Promise<Served<T>>

symbols.name: memoExpire
symbols.sig: export function memoExpire(key: string, ageMs: number, now: () => number = Date.now): void
doc: Marks what is kept under a key as old (just past `ageMs`), so that the next asking is answered from it at once while a new one is made in the background. Does nothing when nothing is kept.

symbols.name: recall
symbols.sig: export function recall<T>(key: string): { value: T; at: number } | null
doc: Returns what is kept under a key, with its time, without asking the source (null when nothing is kept).

symbols.name: remember
symbols.sig: export function remember(key: string, value: unknown, now: () => number = Date.now): void

behaviours: memo: the second asking inside the ttl is the kept answer, nothing is made again
swr: with nothing kept the answer is made while the caller waits
swr: a fresh answer (5 of 10 minutes) is returned at once, no refresh
swr: at 85% of the ttl the OLD answer is returned at once (the caller does not wait for the 200 ms rebuild) and a refresh is started and scheduled
swr: while a refresh is running another asking gets the old answer and starts no second refresh
swr: once the background refresh is done, the new answer is what is served (n2), fresh again
swr: a stale answer (past the ttl) is still returned at once, with a refresh behind it
swr: a refresh that fails does not lose the old answer, and does not throw into the caller
swr: an answer older than the limit (here 3 hours) is made again with the caller waiting
swr: too old and the source fails: the old answer is returned marked stale (as memo does)
swr: nothing kept and the source fails: the error reaches the caller
a quiet tab (30 minutes) is still fresh after 20: the kept answer, no refresh
a hot tab (5 minutes) is answered from what is kept at 4.5 minutes while a new one is made behind it (refresh-ahead at 80% of 5)
a tab expired on demand is still answered at once (the old one, not a wait for the rebuild), a new one is made in the background, and the next asking has it
expiring what is not kept does nothing
